relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: In galcanezumab-treated animals (n = 32), the stimulated increase in CGRP release was 184.50 ± 7.60%, which was significantly different from the vehicle group

relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 receptor activation-induced SP release was more intense after anti-CGRP antibody treatment in both sexes and the difference was significant in females.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP (10 μM) increased the histamine release to 134.9 ± 7.5% (n = 5) of the basal release

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Galcanezumab treatment also reduced the amount of histamine released from dural mast cells upon stimulation with CGRP

key_findings: Fluorophore-labelled galcanezumab persisted in dura mater vessels and trigeminal ganglion up to 30 days; it reduced capsaicin-evoked CGRP release (females) and increased SP release.
Galcanezumab blunted CGRP-induced but not compound 48/80-induced histamine release; somatostatin release unchanged.
